title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes a space through its poset of 'figures', which he calls an 'atelier' with axioms At1–At7, a relation ≤ ('subfigure') and a second relation ≪. On the previous page he defines a sub-atelier as a non-empty, downward-closed part F' of F, stable under sups.

This page restarts the definitions in purely order-theoretic terms.

(1) A crossed-out definition. For a poset (F,≤), a closed (i.e. downward-closed) part F' is 'ample' if it is non-empty (equivalently it contains the least element φ_F) and is stable under sups of families bounded in F'. It is 'spacieuse' if it is stable under all sups of families bounded in F.

(2) The retained text. Let (F,≤) satisfy At1: every bounded family has a sup, and there is a least element φ_F. Let F' be a lower set.
- F' is non-empty iff φ_F ∈ F'.
- If a family (F_i) in F' is bounded in F' by G, then its sup F in F satisfies F ≤ G, hence F ∈ F' since F' is downward closed. F is then also the sup in F'.
- So F' again satisfies At1, and the inclusion F' → F preserves the sups that exist in F'.

(3) Let M be the set of (strictly) irreducible elements of F. These are the completely join-irreducible elements: F = sup F_i implies F = F_i for some i. Taking the empty family, φ_F is excluded. Set M' = M ∩ F'.
- Claim: M' is exactly the set of irreducibles of F'.
- Proof: the families bounded by F are the same whether computed in F or in F', and so are their sups. Hence the irreducibility condition is identical in both.

The next page shows that At2 (every element is the sup of the irreducibles below it) also passes to F'. It then takes F = P(I), where lower sets of finite subsets are abstract simplicial complexes on I, and 'spacieux' ones are just P(I').

Purpose: to show that downward-closed sub-objects ('sub-ateliers', the analogue of subcomplexes or closed subspaces) inherit the axioms, as a step in building a combinatorial or tame topology from posets of figures.
errors: No mathematical error. The argument is correct for lower sets in a bounded-complete poset with bottom.

Precision: 'F' → F commute aux sup' should be read only for families bounded in F'. A family in F' that is bounded in F but not in F' need not have its F-sup in F'. That is exactly the gap between 'ample' and 'spacieux', which Grothendieck himself separates.

ideas.what: A downward-closed subset of a bounded-complete poset with least element is again bounded-complete, and the inclusion preserves bounded sups.
ideas.modern_name: Lower sets (order ideals) of bounded-complete posets / Scott domains are bounded-complete.

ideas.what: Completely join-irreducible elements of a lower set F' are exactly the join-irreducibles of F lying in F'.
ideas.modern_name: Completely join-irreducible elements and their restriction to order ideals

ideas.what: Distinction between 'ample' (stable under sups bounded in F') and 'spacieux' (stable under all sups existing in F) for closed sub-parts. This is the analogue of subcomplex versus full sub-poset closed under joins.
ideas.modern_name: Order ideal versus join-closed (complete) ideal; abstract simplicial complex versus principal ideal in P(I)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in order theory and combinatorial topology

missed.claim: The page is a routine verification within Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 attempt to found 'analysis situs' on posets of figures ('ateliers', axioms At1–At7 with relations ≤ and ≪). The atelier framework as a whole does not appear in the published literature. This particular page contains only standard order theory.
missed.quote: Donc F' (il satisfait donc At 1) est stable par sup. majorés dans F', et F' ↪ F commute aux sup.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only as documentation of the structure of Grothendieck's tame-topology programme, which is related to themes of the Esquisse d'un programme. No new result here.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary order-theoretic lemma: lower sets inherit bounded-completeness and join-irreducibles. It is standard, and is noteworthy only as part of the unpublished 'atelier' axiomatics.
transcription_corrections: '(i.e. satisf. Ab 1)' should read 'At 1' (atelier axiom 1), consistent with At1–At7 on p.38 and At 2 on p.40.
'éléments (Ab$^+$) irréductibles' is likely '(str.) irréductibles', i.e. strictement irréductibles, as on p.38 '(strictement) irréductibles'. Likewise '(Ab.) irréd.' should be '(str.) irréd.'.
In the struck definition, 'stable par Sup. majorés dans F'' contrasts with 'stable par Sup. majorés dans F' for 'spacieuse'. The words 'dans' are underlined in the manuscript to mark this contrast.
'Alors dans F' [?] est non vide' is better read as 'Alors F' est non vide ssi φ_F ∈ F''.
